memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: From that land he went to Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah and Resen, which is between Nineveh and Calah - which is the great city. - Gen 10:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Nimrod keeps building - city after city, Nineveh, Calah, and more, described here as "the great city." He was a tireless founder of civilisation, leaving his mark across the land. On the surface, this is impressive achievement: cities rising, kingdoms expanding, a name being made. Yet these very cities - Babylon, Nineveh - would become in Scripture symbols of human power arrayed against God.

There is a quiet warning woven into this list of building projects. It is possible to build much and yet build without God. Nimrod's cities were monuments to human might and ambition, testaments to what people can achieve when they set their minds to greatness. But greatness that leaves God out, however grand, is building on sand.

We live in a culture of builders - building careers, reputations, businesses, platforms, legacies. None of these things is wrong in itself. But the crucial question is whether God is at the centre of what we build, or merely left out while we make a name for ourselves.

The Psalmist reminds us: "Unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labor in vain" (Ps 127:1). All our building, if God is not in it, is ultimately empty, however impressive it looks. Nineveh and Babylon are ruins now; only what is built with God endures. So build your life, your work, your family - but build it with God, on the foundation that lasts, Jesus Christ (1 Cor 3:11). Then your labour will not be in vain.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is God at the centre of what you are building, or left out?
- What are you building that will actually last?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, unless You build with me, all my labour is in vain. Be the centre and foundation of everything I build, so that my life's work is not empty monuments but lasting fruit for Your glory.
